subject: Mental Models
title: Breaking Problems Down
description: A quick win: understand Breaking Problems Down.

hook.text: Eating an elephant seems impossible. But the old riddle says: one bite at a time. Decomposition is that bite.

buildup.text: Decomposition splits a complex problem into smaller, manageable sub-problems. Solve each piece and the whole follows.

discovery.text: Software engineers do this instinctively. A million-line codebase is just thousands of small functions working together.

twist.text: The hardest part is knowing where to cut. Bad decomposition creates new problems at the seams between pieces.

climax.text: Cut along natural joints. Find the places where sub-problems have minimal overlap and clean interfaces.

punchline.text: Big problems are just small problems stacked. Find the seams.

quiz.question: What is the biggest risk when decomposing a problem?
options: Cutting in the wrong places and creating new problems at the seams
Spending too much time on planning
